question: Which of the following dams was NOT funded during the First Five-Year Plan for development of irrigation facility?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gosi Khurd dam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gosi Khurd dam was not part of the First Five-Year Plan in India, which spanned from 1951 to 1956.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan focused primarily on large-scale projects like Bhakra Nangal, Hirakud, and Mettur dams for improving irrigation and power generation.
 
• Gosi Khurd dam, located on the Wainganga river in Maharashtra, was sanctioned later and not during the First Five-Year Plan.
 
• The development of irrigation facilities during the First Five-Year Plan was crucial for India's agricultural sector and aimed at increasing food production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956)**

 
 
• Launched by the Government of India with an emphasis on agricultural development.
 
• The plan aimed at addressing the severe food shortages in post-independence India.
 
• Significant investments were made in irrigation projects to boost agricultural productivity.
 
• It prioritized the construction of major dams like Bhakra Nangal, Hirakud, and Mettur.
 
 
 
• **Bhakra Nangal Dam**
 
 
• Located on the Sutlej river in Himachal Pradesh and Punjab.
 
• One of India's earliest and largest multi-purpose dams.
 
• Key objectives included irrigation, flood control, and hydroelectric power generation.
 
 
 
• **Hirakud Dam**
 
 
• Constructed on the Mahanadi river in Odisha.
 
• Recognized as the longest earthen dam in the world at the time of construction.
 
• Primarily aimed at flood control, irrigation, and power generation.
 
 
 
• **Mettur Dam**
 
 
• Built on the Cauvery river in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is one of the oldest and largest dams in India.
 
• Serves as a major source for irrigation, drinking water, and power generation.
